question:
Find the median from the following data.

 
 

 Age in years
 15-25
 25-35
 35-45
 45-55
 <td st
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **Total Frequency** (N) = 170, so N/2 = 85.

Calculate **Cumulative Frequency** (CF) until it reaches or exceeds 85: 11, 29, 51, 81 (for 45-55), 121 (for 55-65).

Since 85 lies in the 55-65 class, **Median Class** = 55-65.

Median = Lower Limit + [(Required remaining frequency ÷ Class frequency) × Class width].

Median = 55 + [(85 − 81) ÷ 40] × 10 = 55 + 1 = 56 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 56 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Class Intervals (Age):** 15-25, 25-35, 35-45, 45-55, 55-65, 65-75, 75-85

**Frequencies (f):** 11, 18, 22, 30, 40, 16, 33

**Formula Used:**

Median = L + [((N/2) − cf) ÷ f] × h

Where L = Lower limit of median class, N = Total frequency, cf = Cumulative frequency of preceding class, f = Frequency of median class, h = Class width.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6dff092c86d630cf5c8c3b28641b39b174a46f4279065867c1fabecfbc31a2bc.png] 

**Step-by-step Calculation:**

⇒ **Total Frequency (N)** = 11 + 18 + 22 + 30 + 40 + 16 + 33 = 170

⇒ **N/2** = 170 ÷ 2 = 85

⇒ **Cumulative Frequencies (CF):**

15-25: 11 | 25-35: 29 | 35-45: 51 | 45-55: 81 | 55-65: 121

⇒ Since 81 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode is: Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean.

Median of Grouped Data

The median is the value that divides the data into two equal halves. It is calculated using the formula L + [((N/2) − cf) ÷ f] × h.

Cumulative Frequency Types

There are two types: 'Less than' type (adding frequencies from top) and 'More than' type (adding frequencies from bottom).</p
